questions.question: If 15 July 2002 is a Monday, then what will be the day of the week on 16 October 2005?
questions.solution:
**Given :** 15 July 2002 is a Monday

 
• Total number of days in a normal year = 365
 
• Number of odd days in a normal year = 365 ÷ 7 = 1
 
• Total number of days in a leap year = 366
 
• Number of odd days in a leap year = 366 ÷ 7 = 2
 
• 15 July 2002 (Monday) + 1 odd day (2003) + 2 odd days (2004) + 1 odd day (2005) = 15 July 2005 (Friday)
 
• Total number of days from 15 July 2005 to 16 October 2005 = 16 (July) + 31 (August) + 30 (September) + 16 (October) = 93
 
• Total number of odd days from 15 July 2005 to 16 October 2005 = 93 ÷ 7 = 2
 
• Now starting from 15 July 2005, every 7th day will be a Friday.
 
• Therefore, Friday + 2 = **16 October 2005 i.e., Sunday**

Hence, **'option 1' **is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number.

64 : 18 :: 196 : 24 :: 529 : ?
questions.solution:
**Logic : Square root of first number + 10 = second number**

1) 64 : 18

⇒ √64 + 10 

⇒ 8 + 10 = 18

And,

2) 196 : 24 

⇒ √196 + 10 

⇒ 14 + 10 = 24

Similarly,

3) 529 : ?

⇒ **√**529 + 10

⇒ 23 + 10 = 33

Hence, the correct answer is **"33".**

questions.question:
Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All cakes are sweets.

No sweet is a biscuit.

Some chocolates are biscuits.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some biscuits are cakes.

II. Some chocolates are sweets.

III. No cake is a chocolate.

options.text: Both conclusions I and III follow
Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
**The least possible Venn diagram:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3f535a564414ee3ea32d825c213731ad9a37ba77e53cffa93c6a46df77a845f0.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. Some biscuits are cakes → **False** (As no sweet is a biscuit and all cakes are sweets. So some biscuits are cakes is not true)

II. Some chocolates are sweets → **False **(As no sweet is a biscuit and some chocolates are biscuits. So some chocolates sweets is not true)

III. No cake is a chocolate → **False** (There is no direct relation between cake and chocolate. So, it may or may not be true. Hence, this is considered false).

Hence, the correct answer is **"****N****one of the conclusions follow"**.

If ‘A’ denotes ‘+’, ‘B’ denotes ‘×’, ‘C’ denotes ‘–’ and ‘D’ denotes ‘÷’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation?

(84 D 14) A 17 C 13 B (75 D 15) A 9 B 7 = ?
questions.solution:
**BODMAS Rule:**

 [IMAGE: https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/Ro308yDlMHZMoSnguV0wigWvPaVi44cD_wvabas7GQSDUI6EkfsS8WmcEjL6IMM8JHFvk9NUSyyPnObrQ7-yvuy4-15yELDTWsJUg68JE9ziEIXR4IjDG2Xd9k7OgV4KeTh8vfHj] 

**Explanation : **

 
 

 
 
**Letter**

 
 
 
**Symbol**

 
 
 

 
 
A

 
 
 
+

 
 
 

 
 
B

 
 
 
**×**

 
 
 

 
 
C

 
 
 
-

 
 
 

 
 
D

 
 
 
÷

 
 
 

If we apply BODMAS rule on the given equation

⇒ (84 D 14) A 17 C 13 B (75 D 15) A 9 B 7

**⇒ (84 ÷ 14)** + 17 - 13 ×__**( 75 ÷ 15 )**__ + 9 ×** **7

⇒ 6 + 17 - __**13 × 5**__ + __**9 × 7**__

⇒ __**6 + 17**__ - 65 __**+ 63**__

⇒ __**86 - 65**__

⇒ 21

Hence, **21 **is the** correct answer.**
